verdicts.trueWording: European story uses triads; Native American story does things in fours
verdicts.note: p.88 verbatim: 'European story uses triads; Native American story is more likely to do things in fours.' Page says 'do things in fours'; claim's 'group events in fours' is supported by the preceding clause 'grouping events into similar, accumulative semirepetitions'.

verdicts.trueWording: Each repetition both builds the foundation and advances the story
verdicts.note: p.88 verbatim: 'Each repetition both builds the foundation of the climactic event, and advances the story.' Sits inside the oral-narrative paragraph ('In oral narrative, which generally maintains many formal elements...'), so the 'in oral narrative' limb is supported by context.

verdicts.trueWording: as simple as a rhythm can be: two beats. Stress, release
verdicts.note: p.88 verbatim, with both remaining limbs on the same page: 'Stress, release' and 'but on so vast a scale'. 'Master rhythm' is Le Guin's own term on p.89 ('the devices by which Tolkien establishes this master rhythm in the Trilogy').

verdicts.trueWording: readers encouraged to see story as a road, driven fast, no stops
verdicts.note: p.88: 'readers have been encouraged to look at a story as a road we're driving, well paved and graded and without detours, on which we go as fast as we possibly can, with no changes of pace and certainly no stops'. Quote matches word for word (page uses a curly apostrophe in 'we're'). 'Modern' = 'Increasingly, during the past century'.

verdicts.trueWording: Phrases describing the hill country, the scent of turf, the quality of the light
verdicts.note: p.90 verbatim, and it is an entry in the list introduced on p.89 as 'These are the chief recurrent elements I listed', so the 'recurrent elements' limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: Mention of the compass directions - frequent, often benign or malign
verdicts.note: p.90 verbatim: 'Mention of the compass directions—frequent, and often with a benign or malign connotation', listed among the chapter's chief recurrent elements.

verdicts.trueWording: I believe there is no moment when we don't know, literally, where north is
verdicts.note: p.91 verbatim (curly apostrophe in 'don't'). Preceded by 'Directionality is extremely important all though the book', supporting the 'in the book' limb. Le Guin hedges with 'I believe', which the claim's 'claims' fairly reflects.

verdicts.trueWording: I went through the chapter noting every major image, event, and feeling-tone
verdicts.note: p.89 verbatim, continuing '...and particularly noting recurrences or strong similarity of words, phrases, scenes, actions, feelings, and images.' The one-chapter limb is supported by 'I narrowed my scope to one chapter, the eighth of volume 1'.

verdicts.trueWording: Very soon, sooner than I expected, repetitions began to emerge
verdicts.note: p.89 verbatim: 'Very soon, sooner than I expected, repetitions began to emerge, including a positive/negative binary pattern of alternation or reversal.' Both limbs (the pattern, and its emerging sooner than expected) are in the same sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: The tremendous landscape of Middle Earth is built up by repetition... and reversal
verdicts.note: p.95 verbatim: 'The tremendous landscape of Middle Earth, the psychological and moral universe of The Lord of the Rings, is built up by repetition, semirepetition, suggestion, foreshadowing, recollection, echo, and reversal.'

verdicts.trueWording: These few lines... are full of rapid reversals
verdicts.note: p.94 verbatim, immediately following 'These are the final sentences:' and the quoted Tolkien passage, so the 'chapter's final sentences' limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: Yet the tone is quiet, the language simple
verdicts.note: p.94 verbatim. The 'drumbeat' limb is supported two sentences earlier: the reversals 'are like drumbeats', and 'Yet' carries the concessive 'despite'.

verdicts.trueWording: Great novels offer us not only a series of events, but a place
verdicts.note: p.94 verbatim, continuing 'a landscape of the imagination which we can inhabit and return to' - every limb of the claim is in that one sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: The rhythmic structure of narrative is both journeylike and architectural.
verdicts.note: p.94 verbatim, the whole sentence, preceded by 'I think it is a mistake to think of story as simply moving forward.'

verdicts.trueWording: Le Guin's thesis is simple: ...as simple as a rhythm can be: two beats
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture of kate_nepveu's 2006-06-04 post 'LotR re-read: Le Guin, "Rhythmic Pattern in The Lord of the Rings"' fetched at HTTP 200. The post writes 'Le Guin's thesis is simple:' and then block-quotes the passage containing 'as simple as a rhythm can be: two beats. Stress, release.' Every limb (Nepveu, summarising the essay, quoting the thesis) is on the raw page.
